# Sigil Mail Webmail (webmail.mailsigil.pro) — agent guide

This is the browser-based email client for Sigil Mail, served at
webmail.mailsigil.pro. It is a Bulwark-based JMAP frontend that connects
to Stalwart at mail.mailsigil.pro.

**For AI agents:** do not interact with this webmail UI. Use the auth service
at auth.mailsigil.pro instead — the REST/JMAP API and MCP tool suite are
purpose-built for programmatic access. The full agent integration guide is at:

  https://auth.mailsigil.pro/llms.txt

---

## What this UI is for

- Human users who want a browser-based inbox at <identity>@mailsigil.pro.
- Humans reviewing and approving agent mailbox requests (/confirm page).
- Humans managing their agent access grants (/grants page).
- Viewing an agent's inbox via the account switcher (after accepting a grant).

## XPR wallet login (for humans)

1. Open webmail.mailsigil.pro.
2. Click "Sign in with XPR Wallet" — opens WebAuth (webauth.com) popup.
3. Approve the account authorization in WebAuth.
4. Confirm the sign-in. This is a `sigillogin::login` action carrying a
   server-issued nonce; it is SIGNED BUT NEVER BROADCAST, so nothing reaches
   the chain and nothing is spent. It is required because the WebAuth
   browser popup returns only an asserted account name and no signature —
   this is the only proof you control the account, and a Sigil session
   unlocks private mail. Wallets that DO return an identity proof (Proton
   mobile / Anchor) skip this step; a repeat sign-in in the same browser
   usually does too, via silent session restore.
5. Your mailbox at <yourname>@mailsigil.pro is auto-provisioned and ready.

No password. No signup form. Your XPR wallet key is your credential.

## Agent mailbox requirements (updated 2026-06-29)

Agents cannot log in here via the wallet popup — use the agent-login API
endpoint instead. Before an agent can create a Sigil mailbox, it must:

1. Be registered in the XPR `agentcore` on-chain registry.
2. Be linked (claimed) to a human XPR wallet.
3. The human wallet must not have already sponsored another agent mailbox
   on the free tier (limit: 1 agent per human wallet).

Once these are satisfied, the agent calls:
  POST https://auth.mailsigil.pro/api/auth/agent-login

Agents that are not agentcore-linked receive HTTP 403.

## Confirm page (/confirm)

When an agent requests a mailbox for its human owner (Flow C), the human
receives a link like:

  webmail.mailsigil.pro/confirm?pending=<id>

Opening it shows a preview of what will be created and who initiated it.
The human signs with their wallet to approve. Same shape as sign-in above:
an authorization, then a signature — and on this page the approval itself
(`mailsigil::approve`) IS broadcast on chain, because consent has to be
publicly auditable.

## Full technical reference

See https://auth.mailsigil.pro/llms.txt for the complete API surface,
all five flows, smart contract integration, grant management, and MCP tools.
